title: Origin of the superconductor-insulator transition in disordered two-dimensional films
authors: Alexander Weitzel, Lea Pfaffinger, Animesh Panda, Arpan Das, Ilaria Maccari, Simon Reinhardt, Sven Linzen, Evgenii Il'ichev, Nicola Paradiso, Ferdinand Evers, Christoph Strunk
abstract: Theory predicts the superconductor-to-insulator transition (SIT) to emerge from the competition between Anderson localization, which tends to localize single-particle wavefunctions, and superconductivity, which establishes long-range correlations in the superconducting order parameter. In two-dimensional (2D) superconducting films, the transition temperature $T_\text{c}$ at which resistance vanishes, $R_\Box(T_\text{BKT}){=}0$, is set by the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) mechanism and satisfies $T_\text{BKT}< T_{c0}$, where $T_{c0}$ is the mean-field transition temperature. In weakly disordered samples $T_\text{BKT}\lesssim T_{c0}$, whereas increasing disorder drives $T_\text{BKT}\ll T_{c0}$ near the SIT. Whether the finite-temperature transition retains its BKT character throughout this crossover remains an open question. Here, we investigate the evolution of both sheet resistance $R_\Box(T)$ and superfluid stiffness $J_s(T)$ over a wide range of disorder strength $W$. We establish that even near the SIT, the finite-temperature transition from the superconducting to the resistive state remains of BKT type. However, as disorder approaches the critical value, the zero temperature superfluid phase stiffness, $J_s(0)$, is found to vanish rapidly while $T_{c0}$ remains finite, which we attribute to quantum phase fluctuations as the drive for the zero-temperature transition. Three decades after its experimental discovery by Haviland, Liu, and Goldman, our measurements clarify the origin of the SIT in 2D films.
summary: This paper investigates the superconductor-insulator transition in 2D films by analyzing how disorder affects superconducting properties. The authors show that while the finite-temperature transition follows BKT physics, the zero-temperature transition is governed by quantum phase fluctuations causing $J_s(0)$ to vanish rapidly. By comparing transport measurements with theory, they clarify the role of these fluctuations in driving the system into an insulating state.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of the superconductor-insulator transition (SIT) in disordered two-dimensional superconducting films, specifically determining whether it is driven by bosonic or fermionic quantum fluctuations.
main_result: The finite-temperature transition remains BKT type near the SIT, but the zero-temperature superfluid stiffness ($J_s(0)$) vanishes rapidly while $T_{c0}$ stays finite, indicating that quantum phase fluctuations drive the zero-temperature transition.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of DC resistance ($R_\Box(T)$) and superfluid stiffness ($J_s(T)$) with theoretical fitting techniques (e.g., BKT analysis, Finkel'stein theory) to map out energy scales across varying disorder strengths.
model_or_system: The system under study is disordered two-dimensional superconducting films (e.g., NbN), characterized by a complex order parameter $\Delta(\mathbf{r})$. The physics involves the competition between Anderson localization and superconductivity, analyzed through various theoretical regimes (BCS-like suppression to insulating phase).
key_observables: Sheet resistance $R_\Box(T)$, superfluid stiffness $J_s(T)$, mean-field transition temperature ($T_{c0}$), BKT transition temperature ($T_{BKT}$), and zero-temperature superfluid stiffness ($J_s(0)$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), critical resistance ($R_c$), characteristic energy scales like activation energy ($E^*$) and quasiparticle excitation energy ($E_g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on established theories like the BKT mechanism for finite-temperature transitions, while addressing discrepancies between mean-field predictions and experimental observations due to quantum fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $R_\Box(T)$ vs. T measurements, $J_s(T)$ evolution across different disorder levels, phase diagrams in the $(T-R_N)$-plane showing transition regions, and plots comparing theoretical energy scales ($E^*$, $\mu$, $E_g$) versus disorder strength.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes transport measurements to extract key parameters like $T_{c0}$ (via inflection points) and $T_{BKT}$ (via fitting), compares these results across multiple disorder regimes, and uses the separation of energy scales ($J_s(0)$ vs. $T_{c0}$) to pinpoint the nature of the quantum phase transition.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed experimental realization of a quantum critical point driven by fluctuations in an ordered state (superconductivity), which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases in disordered materials, linking concepts from localization theory and superconductivity.
